questions.question: Which of these countries is NOT a permanent member of the UN Security Council?
questions.hint: The permanent members are often called the P5. This country has asked for a permanent seat for many years, together with Brazil, India and Japan.
questions.explanation: The five permanent members are China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States. Each of them can block a decision with its veto. The Council has 15 members in all: the other ten are elected for two years.

questions.question: In which year was the North Atlantic Treaty, the treaty that created NATO, signed in Washington?
questions.hint: The Soviet blockade of West Berlin was still going on. Later the same year, two German states were founded.
questions.explanation: Twelve countries signed the treaty on 4 April 1949: the United States, Canada and ten countries of Western Europe. 1955 is the year of the Warsaw Pact, the rival alliance led by the Soviet Union.

image.alt: A man signs a paper at a large desk while a group of men in suits stand behind him and watch.

label.title: President Truman signs the document that puts the North Atlantic Treaty into effect

sources.label: US Department of State, Office of the Historian: NATO, 1949

questions.question: What does Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty say?
options: An attack on one member is an attack on all
Each member must spend 2% of its income on defence
New members need the agreement of all members
Members must not go to war with one another
questions.hint: It has been used only once, after the attacks of 11 September 2001 on the United States.
questions.explanation: NATO calls this collective defence, and it is the heart of the treaty. If one member is attacked, each of the others must help it. The treaty itself is short: it has only 14 articles.

questions.question: Which of these countries was NOT one of the six that signed the Treaty of Rome in 1957?
questions.hint: The same six countries had already put their coal and steel industries together a few years earlier.
questions.explanation: Belgium, France, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and West Germany signed the treaty on 25 March 1957. It created the European Economic Community, which later grew into the European Union. The United Kingdom joined only in 1973 and left in 2020.

questions.question: In which city was the Charter of the United Nations signed on 26 June 1945?
questions.hint: Delegates from 50 countries met in this city from April to June 1945. They agreed on the text in its opera house.
questions.explanation: The Charter was signed in San Francisco at the end of a two-month conference. It came into force on 24 October 1945, which is now United Nations Day. The UN built its headquarters in New York a few years later.

questions.question: Which treaty, signed in 1992, created the European Union?
questions.hint: It set the rules for the future single currency, and it made the people of the member countries citizens of the Union.
questions.explanation: Twelve countries signed the treaty in the Dutch city of Maastricht on 7 February 1992, and it came into force on 1 November 1993. The treaties of Amsterdam, Nice and Lisbon came later and changed how the Union works.

questions.question: As of November 2026, which country is the newest member of NATO?
questions.hint: It gave up a long policy of military non-alignment and joined in March 2024.
questions.explanation: Sweden became the 32nd member of NATO on 7 March 2024. Finland had joined eleven months earlier, on 4 April 2023. The two countries applied on the same day, 18 May 2022.

questions.question: As of November 2026, how many member states does the United Nations have?
questions.hint: The newest member is an African country that became independent in 2011.
questions.explanation: South Sudan became the 193rd member on 14 July 2011, and no country has joined since then. The UN started in 1945 with 51 members. The Holy See and Palestine are observer states, not members; with them the total is 195.

questions.question: As of November 2026, which of these European Union countries has kept its own national currency?
questions.hint: Its voters said no to the euro in a referendum in 2000, and the country has a legal opt-out.
questions.explanation: Denmark is the only EU country with an opt-out from the euro. Every other member is expected to adopt it when it is ready. The euro is now the currency of 21 of the 27 EU countries: Bulgaria joined in 2026, Croatia in 2023 and Estonia in 2011.

questions.question: This flag was first adopted in 1955 by an organisation that is not the European Union. Which one?
options: The European Coal and Steel Community
questions.hint: It was founded in 1949 and is based in Strasbourg. It looks after the European Court of Human Rights.
questions.explanation: The Council of Europe is a human rights organisation, separate from the EU and with more member countries. EU leaders adopted the same flag in 1985. The twelve stars are a symbol of unity; the number has nothing to do with the number of members.
